source: It is not the case that, if this evidence is decisive, this doubt is justified. Therefore this evidence is decisive and this doubt is not justified.

reconstruction.title: Negation of Conditional Leading to Conjunction

claims.text: It is not the case that, if this evidence is decisive, this doubt is justified.

evidence.quote: It is not the case that, if this evidence is decisive, this doubt is justified.

claims.interpretation_note: This is a negation of a conditional statement (¬(A → B)), which is logically equivalent to A ∧ ¬B.

claims.text: Therefore this evidence is decisive and this doubt is not justified.

evidence.quote: Therefore this evidence is decisive and this doubt is not justified.

claims.interpretation_note: This is the conclusion derived from the negation of the conditional in c1.

translations.reason: The premise negates the conditional 'if D then J', which is formalized as ¬(D → J) in propositional logic.
The conclusion asserts the conjunction of D and ¬J, which is logically equivalent to the negation of the conditional in c1.
